CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports having been struggling with depression on and off, particularly over the past year due to isolation and remote work. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily, which has helped her in the past. She notes that a lot has been weighing on her lately and feels that increasing her medication dose may help her through this difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that is managed but exacerbated by prolonged sitting at her desk during work. Pain improves with position changes and standing. She denies numbness with tingling or radiating pain down her legs, though she does experience some numbness that feels like her leg is "falling asleep." She is able to perform her activities of daily living but notes that both extremes of sitting and standing for prolonged periods bother her. She reports that her heart has been doing well since her congenital coronary artery bypass grafting performed at a young age, and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Denies distress. Depression: Acknowledged, worsening recently. Neurologic: Denies weakness in legs, denies tingling. Musculoskeletal: Chronic back pain with numbness. Cardiovascular: History of CABG, currently stable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, chronic back pain, congenital coronary artery anomaly s/p CABG.

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works remotely. Reports isolation over the past year.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Appears in no acute distress. Neck: No thyroid enlargement. Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable. Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft. Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased back flexion. Neurologic: Lower extremity strength intact, no edema.

RESULTS
ECG: Unchanged from last year. Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Chronic back pain: Physical therapy referral; offered pain medication but patient prefers to start with physical therapy. History of CABG: Order echocardiogram. Continue aspirin 81 mg daily. Nurse will assist with scheduling tests.
